sources.title: NOAA GHCN-Daily format and flags
sources.use_and_limits: PRCP units are tenths of mm; -9999 is missing. Preserve measurement, quality and source flags; an empty quality flag is not field calibration.

sources.title: USDA NRCS TR-55, Urban Hydrology for Small Watersheds
sources.use_and_limits: USDA primary document hosted by HydroCAD. Equations 2-3/2-4, table 2-2a: good open space (>75% grass cover) A/B/C/D 39/61/74/80; newly graded 77/86/91/94; impervious 98. ARC II, Ia=0.2S. CN classes are selected scenario conditions, not site measurements. Chapter 2 warns on low-runoff estimates; no annual runoff/recharge/peak-flow claim.

sources.title: Microsoft SJ04 fourth revised project description, July 2025
sources.use_and_limits: Printed pp. 9, 15, 20: planned 76.8 MW IT; approximately 680 acre-feet/year recycled cooling supply; CoC 4; sanitary blowdown; 3.5 acre-feet construction water. Design estimates, not observed WUE. Same benchmark used in both demos; neither San Jose connection nor climate is transferred as verified.

sources.title: DOE FEMP: Cooling Tower Management
sources.use_and_limits: Make-up replaces evaporation, blowdown and drift. With negligible drift/leaks, blowdown = make-up/CoC. Liquid cooling inside servers does not by itself specify how heat is rejected outdoors.

sources.title: EPA AP-42 13.2.3: Heavy Construction Operations
sources.use_and_limits: Dust depends on activity, worked area, fine particles, soil moisture and traffic. Source does not establish a forest-versus-field watering multiplier.

sources.title: CEC construction-water conversation for a different San Jose project, 2020
sources.use_and_limits: Printed page 1: about 51 acre-feet total, dust control dominant. Page 2 mentions a rough 1,000 US gallons/acre/day heuristic; not a universal dose or an SJ04 estimate. Converted rate is about 0.935 L/m²/day, used only as a plausibility anchor for the authored 1 L/m²/day demo allowance.

sources.title: EPA: Concrete Washout
sources.use_and_limits: Concrete washwater can have pH near 12 and needs containment. This is the washwater hazard, not a predicted downstream water-body pH.

sources.title: CEC Walsh Data Center initial study, February 2020
sources.use_and_limits: Sections 5.13 and 5.18: air-cooled chillers and 25.6 acre-feet/year operational potable demand. Different demand boundary and capacity: not an isolated technology saving or WUE comparison.

sources.title: FAO: Basic materials for construction
sources.use_and_limits: Concrete contains mixing water; Table 9 gives example mixtures. Does not establish a data-centre concrete volume or certify our assumed 180 L/m³ recipe.

sources.title: User map link: Golden Gate Park Polo Field
sources.use_and_limits: Resolved to Golden Gate Park Polo Field, place point 37.7682117,-122.4932246. This label is not surveyed parcel geometry. Local reproduction reference in raw/location-reference.json.

sources.title: SF Recreation & Parks: Polo Field venue listing
sources.use_and_limits: Venue listing: 24.64 acres (~9.97 ha), not a measured natural-turf or buildable boundary. Checked HTML locally after web-reader timeouts. The 4 ha demo subset is authored.

sources.title: SF Recreation & Parks: official Polo Fields field map
sources.use_and_limits: One-page aerial field map: natural-grass playing pitches within perimeter tracks, surrounding woodland outside. Historical imagery reference (2012 shown), not current survey; cross-checked current facility/usage pages. Image not bundled.

sources.title: NOAA GHCN-Daily San Francisco Downtown USW00023272
sources.use_and_limits: Verbatim December 2014 PRCP line retained; day 11 value 864 tenths mm = 86.4 mm, blank measurement/quality flags, source W. Daily gauge depth approximately 5.8 km east, not field rain or historical measured runoff.

sources.title: NOAA SF Downtown 1991–2020 monthly precipitation normals
sources.use_and_limits: Metric monthly normals, rounded sum 581.4 mm. Annual report 22.89 in = 581.406 mm; rounding only. No annual observed rainfall, annual runoff or cooling-weather simulation.

sources.title: NOAA station metadata, San Francisco Downtown
sources.use_and_limits: Station point 37.7705,-122.4269, elevation 45.7 m. Different microclimate from western park; fog deposition not added.

sources.title: SF Recreation & Parks: Golden Gate Park Master Plan, objectives/policies
sources.use_and_limits: Historical 2005 park context mentions fragile sandy soil; not Polo Fields HSG or measured engineered turf infiltration. Group B chosen for demo, A/C/D alternatives supplied.

sources.title: SFPUC Westside Enhanced Water Recycling Project, FAQ Aug 2024
sources.use_and_limits: Two pages: delivery scheduled end 2026; groundwater backup at Central Pump Station; signage may precede delivery. Does not establish Polo meter demand or data-centre service.

sources.title: SFPUC Westside recycling project status
sources.use_and_limits: Retrieved 2026-10-24: page still lists construction, end 2026. Do not infer that park recycling is already operational or has capacity allocated to a fictional campus.

sources.title: SFPUC Stormwater Management Requirements
sources.use_and_limits: Local requirements depend on combined versus separate service and project conditions. We have not verified this footprint’s drainage connections. Volume-only demo tank is not compliant drainage design and does not predict a named lake/ocean discharge.

sources.title: SF Recreation & Parks: Polo Field facility and usage
sources.use_and_limits: Current facility description identifies athletic grounds and tracks. Companion https://sfrecpark.org/526/Polo-Field-Usage documents rain-saturation closures. Sports turf does not prove unimpeded infiltration or a dry dusty field.

sources.title: SFPUC regional water system: sources, treatment and distribution
sources.use_and_limits: Checked 2026-10-24. Regional context: residents/businesses share a system of sources including Hetch Hetchy, treatment, storage and distribution. This does not identify the fictional campus connection, local spare capacity, peak demand, household shortage, source-specific marginal depletion or required upgrade. Scenario pathway and capacity explanations are qualitative interpretations of system components.
